steps.narration: Welcome to Recursion! Recursion is the art of solving a computational problem by having a function call itself on a strictly smaller subproblem. Think of Russian nesting dolls (Matryoshka): every doll contains an identical, smaller doll inside, until you finally reach the solid, indivisible core—the Base Case!

board_commands.latex: n! = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } n \le 1 \quad \text{(Base Case)} \\ n \times (n-1)! & \text{if } n > 1 \quad \text{(Recursive Step)} \end{cases}

steps.narration: The most critical rule in recursive design is the Base Case. Every recursive path MUST have at least one condition that returns directly without a self-call. Without a base case, or if the parameter doesn't converge toward it, calls pile up indefinitely until Python raises RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded!

board_commands.content: The Golden Rule: Mandatory Terminating Base Case

WARNING: if n <= 1: return 1
Missing this condition creates infinite recursion and crashes!

check_question.question: What happens in Python if a recursive function fails to define or reach a valid base case?
options: A RecursionError / Stack Overflow occurs when memory limit is exceeded
Python automatically transforms it into an iterative while loop
The interpreter applies tail-call optimization automatically
check_question.explanation: Without a reachable base case, stack frames consume all allocated call stack memory, triggering a RecursionError.

steps.agent_thoughts: Goal: Emphasize the mandatory base case to prevent stack overflow errors.

steps.narration: How does the computer remember where to return? The Call Stack! Each active call allocates an activation record (frame) holding parameters and local state. Because the stack is Last-In, First-Out (LIFO), the deepest call completes first, then unwinds backwards: factorial(1) -> factorial(2) -> factorial(3) -> factorial(4) = 24!

board_commands.content: The Call Stack: Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) Unwinding

board_commands.latex: T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1) = O(n) \text{ time}, \quad S(n) = O(n) \text{ auxiliary call stack space}

check_question.question: In what order do suspended recursive stack frames resolve their return values?
check_question.explanation: Function calls push onto a call stack (LIFO structure); the most recent frame completes and pops first.

steps.narration: Recursion truly shines when dealing with branching structures like trees and graphs. In a Binary Search Tree (BST), an In-Order traversal simply says: traverse(left), process(node), traverse(right). Three lines of recursive code do what would require a complex explicit stack in iteration!

code_action.explanation: In-order recursive traversal visits the left branch, records the value, then visits the right branch.

code_chunks.explanation: In-order recursive traversal visits the left branch, records the value, then visits the right branch.

steps.agent_thoughts: Goal: Show why recursion is natural for trees via in-order traversal.

steps.narration: Mastering recursion means knowing when to use it! Recursion is elegant and intuitive for hierarchical data (trees, graphs, divide-and-conquer). However, each call costs memory on the stack: O(h) space where h is maximum recursion depth. Congratulations! You now understand Base Cases, Call Stacks, and Tree Traversal!

board_commands.content:
✓ Base Case: Halts recursive descent, prevents stack overflow
✓ Call Stack (LIFO): Suspends frames and unwinds from deepest call
✓ Auxiliary Space: O(h) stack depth memory overhead
✓ Ideal Applications: Trees, Divide-and-Conquer, Graph DFS

check_question.explanation: Each pending recursive invocation retains an activation frame on the call stack until returned, costing O(depth) memory.
